subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finserve.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the quick call today. Recap + next steps below so we have alignment before the technical sizing session: 

High-level ask
- FinServe wants predictable throughput for real-time assistant features (customer support triage + internal knowledge search).
- Strong preference for Dedicated capacity (isolation + committed throughput).

Usage & SLOs (as discussed)
- Peak TPS target: 40 requests/sec (in the busiest hour).
- Average request size: ~600 tokens in (prompt + context), expected output ~120 tokens.
- Target latency: p50 ~200-300ms, p95 <700ms for text-generation endpoints.
- Concurrent active sessions: ~150 active users during peak (not strict concurrency, but long-tail sessions).

Deployment constraints
- Region: us-west preferred (data residency).
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed KMS planned.

Open sizing questions for the infra call (please confirm):
1) Preferred GPU family: A100 vs H100? You indicated cost sensitivity but helpful to confirm if H100 is acceptable for the latency targets or prefer A100 to lower cost.
2) Token mix: What percentage of requests are short queries (<128 tokens) vs long context (500-2k tokens)? We used 70/30 short/long in our rough model; please correct.
3) Batching tolerance: Are 200-500ms additional latency acceptable if batching reduces cost ~25%?
4) KV cache behavior: How often do users repeat context across sessions (helps cache hit modeling)?

Proposed next steps
- Can we schedule a 45-min technical sizing call with your infra/ML engineer and Rafael this week? Rafael will run a quick capacity model with both A100 and H100 cost/latency tradeoffs.
- I attached the draft Dedicated pricing + a sample capacity worksheet for your team to populate.

Attachments:
- redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing + terms summary)
- finserve_proposed_capacity.xlsx (worksheet for expected TPS/token mix)

Thanks — looking forward to the sizing call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finserve.com>

Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finserve.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- The 40 TPS peak is correct for the main customer-facing assistant. We also have a secondary internal assistant with ~5 TPS peak that can be routed differently.
- Token mix: looks closer to 60% short (<128), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (512-2000).
- Latency tolerance: p95 target should be <500ms if possible; some leeway for background tasks but customer-facing must be lower.
- GPU preference: procurement will push for A100 initially for cost, but engineering (Tom) would like to see H100 numbers if performance gains justify it.
- Batching: For customer-facing flows we prefer lower latency over aggressive batching; background ops can tolerate batching.

We're good to have Rafael and Aditya join the sizing call. How about Wed 15 Jul at 10:30am PT?

Emma
Emma Johnson
Head of Product, FinServe
emma.johnson@finserve.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks Emma — helpful details. A couple of notes from a runtime perspective before the call: 
- With the token mix you provided (60/30/10) and 40 TPS peak, our ballpark for A100 (80GB) is ~2 x A100 nodes to hit p95<500ms with conservative batching disabled for customer paths. H100 can reduce that to 1-1.5 nodes depending on model variant.
- Model variant: Are you planning to use an instruction-tuned 7B/13B or a larger 70B? The GPU sizing differs materially.
- Prefetch + KV caching: if you can share expected session stickiness (how many requests reuse prior context within 5 minutes), we can model cache hit improvements - this often halves effective token compute for long contexts.

I'll bring a short spreadsheet with both A100/H100 scenarios and cost proformas.

Rafael
Principal Infrastructure Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
